decision.recommended_next_phase: Phase 3D.3 - next public candidate source-data intake
decision.result_interpretation: Phase 3D.2A tested the local open-source export route rather than leaving it as a vague TODO. LabPlot 2.12.1 can be installed on this Mac, but its command-line help only opens files/projects, its embedded Origin import strings advertise OPJ rather than OPJU, and an offscreen attempt to open the Saha Fig. 2c/d OPJU timed out in GUI/dialog behavior without producing CSV. The Saha source package remains useful and public, but local table export is blocked without Origin/Origin Viewer on Windows, a working OPJU-capable GUI export, or an open-format mirror.

external_routes.route: Origin or Origin Viewer on Windows
external_routes.notes: OriginLab documents worksheet access in Origin Viewer and Windows Viewer CSV export, but this Mac does not have the Windows toolchain or Origin.
The tool is useful provenance for an eventual Windows/Origin export script, but its published requirements are Windows 11, Origin 2024b, and Origin's Python integration.
Installed through Homebrew and probed locally. The bundled CLI exposes open/project options only; embedded strings identify Origin OPJ import, not OPJU CSV export.
The Saha files are public, but uploading research artifacts to a third-party converter is not an authoritative or repo-reproducible scientific export path without explicit user approval.
